verdicts.reason: A is the original's centred stack shrunk into a 320x50 strip: the headline is tiny, the CTA pill is jammed against the bottom edge, and the wide sides are left empty, so it doesn't suit a banner. B uses the width, but the CTA sits first on the left, so you read the action before the headline, and the headline floats off-centre with dead space on the right.

A has the same cramped centred stack: small headline, CTA touching the bottom edge, empty sides. B reads properly left to right, with a larger headline on the left and the CTA pill on the right, and it keeps the brand colours and serif font. Its only flaw is the awkward line break 'and a / little sunshine.'
